sources.title: Dipolar Poisson-Boltzmann Equation: Ions and Dipoles Close to Charged Surfaces
sources.authentication: Retrieved PDF visibly labels itself arXiv:0705.1269v1, 9 May 2007; title and authors checked.
sources.locator: Eqs. (4)-(5), p. 2: orientation trace and Langevin mean; Eq. (11), p. 2: constrained lattice free energy; text following Eq. (13), p. 3: density saturation.
sources.extraction: Full formula text inspected through web PDF extraction.
sources.result_used: Fixed-magnitude orientational trace generates a Langevin mean moment. Variable mobile density is an additional factor; packing constraints are required to bound total local density.
sources.dictionary: The report separately assumes fixed local density and defines u=b times the mean normalized orientation. Its Legendre transform and subtraction of u^2/(2K) are derived in the report.
sources.application_verdict: Verified for the orientational constitutive model; inapplicable as a derivation of gravitational source normalization or the target remainder.

sources.title: The electrostatic Born-Infeld equations with integrable charge densities
sources.authentication: PDF header and versioned arXiv abstract page checked; both identify v2.
sources.locator: p. 1, abstract: variational functional and associated electrostatic Euler-Lagrange equation.
sources.extraction: Full formula text inspected through web PDF extraction.
sources.result_used: The normalized Born-Infeld density is 1-sqrt(1-|D v|^2), with constitutive derivative D v/sqrt(1-|D v|^2).
sources.dictionary: D v in this PDE paper denotes the potential gradient, not electric displacement. Set its magnitude to u/b and multiply the density by b^2/K for the report's deliberately favorable constitutive analogy.
sources.application_verdict: Verified as a constitutive density; no use of the paper's regularity theorem. Physical identification with gravitational polarization remains an assumption and fails the target endpoint comparison.

sources.title: Steric Effects in Electrolytes: A Modified Poisson-Boltzmann Equation
sources.version: Published PRL 79, 435-438, 21 July 1997; parallel preprint arXiv:cond-mat/9803258v1, 21 March 1998.
sources.authentication: Publisher metadata and publisher fulltext header agree; arXiv preprint title/authors/version checked. The regenerated preprint has a 2024 TeX date; it is not a new research revision.
sources.locator: Eq. (2): ion and solvent mixing entropy; Eq. (5): bounded, Fermi-like high-field occupancy; text below Eq. (2): single-site exclusion interpretation.
sources.extraction: Publisher text and arXiv PDF formula text inspected.
sources.result_used: Finite packing gives finite occupancy through mixing entropy; maximum occupancy does not require the report's logarithmically divergent mechanical energy.
sources.dictionary: The report independently specializes to a binary site with m=2theta-1. Occupancy is not automatically the vector polarization P in the action.
sources.application_verdict: Verified for a finite-capacity statistical mechanism; inapplicable as a selection of n or a derivation of the gravitational source operator.

sources.title: Finite field-energy and interparticle potential in logarithmic electrodynamics
sources.authentication: Publisher HTML title, author list, date and formula numbering checked.
sources.result_used: At B=0 the constitutive potential is -beta^2 log(1-E^2/(2beta^2)) and D=E/(1-E^2/(2beta^2)).
sources.dictionary: Set b=sqrt(2) beta, E=u, divide by K. Subtract the quadratic as required by the repository action.
sources.application_verdict: Verified as an explicit logarithmic constitutive counterexample to 'a logarithm/pole is enough'; it is itself a posited effective electromagnetic model, not the requested microscopic derivation.
